explanation: Rule #1 of branching: Start from the latest clean code.
tip: `git switch main && git pull` before every `git switch -c`.

explanation: Main is sacred. Feature branches are where experiments and development happen.
tip: Set up GitHub branch protection rules to enforce this.

explanation: Memorize this cycle: Issue → Branch → Code → PR → Review → Merge → Pull.
tip: This is what you will do in every software job.

explanation: Status tells you what is clean, modified, staged, and untracked.
One commit per logical change. Don't mix frontend styling with backend database fixes in one commit.
tip: Atomic commits make reading git logs a joy.

explanation: `git revert` is the professional way to undo bugs on shared branches.
tip: Never force push to main in a team project.

explanation: Despite the name, `git blame` is about understanding context and asking the right person for guidance.
tip: GitHub web also has a 'Blame' button on every file view.

explanation: Stashing is your safety net when an urgent interruption happens mid-task.
tip: `git stash` to save, `git stash pop` to resume.

explanation: Recruiters and senior engineers judge your code hygiene as much as the code itself.
tip: A clean GitHub profile opens doors to internships and jobs.

explanation: Version control is not a chore — it is your superpower. Welcome to the Git & GitHub developer community!
tip: Keep building, keep committing, and keep collaborating with HCC!
